title: Level 1 (Beginner) - A-11
notes:
South begins with only 6 top tricks (1 in spades, 2 in hearts, and 3 in diamonds). 3 additional tricks can easily be developed in clubs once the ♣A is dislodged.

There is only one slight problem. The defense might be in a position to take the setting trick in spades when they gain the lead with the ♣A. South can increase his chances of success by allowing West to win the first trick. West will continue spades, but South should hold up his ♠A until the third round.

When East wins his ♣A he has no spades left to play and South has his nine tricks. The contract would still be secure if the defensive spades were divided 4-4. In this case, East would have a spade to return upon winning the ♣A, but the defense would only have 4 tricks available.

If West was dealt 5 spades and the ♣A, there is nothing South can do. The contract will always fail on that lie of the cards.
